chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Isa ibn al-Sariy, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Narrate to me about that upon which the pillars of Islam are built, so that when I adhere to it, my deeds will be purified and the ignorance of what I do not know after it will not harm me.'

So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony that there is no god except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the affirmation of what he brought from Allah, and the right in wealth of Zakat, and the Wilayah which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded, which is the Wilayah of the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).'
For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever dies and does not know his Imam, dies a death of ignorance (Jahiliyyah).'
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority from among you.'
So it was Ali (peace be upon him), then after him it became Hasan, then after him Husayn, then after him Ali ibn Husayn, then after him Muhammad ibn Ali.
Then the matter remains thus. The earth does not become correct except with an Imam, and whoever dies without knowing his Imam dies a death of ignorance.
And the neediest of what one of you will be to his recognition is when his soul reaches here.
He said, and he pointed with his hand to his chest, saying at that time: 'I was upon a good matter.'
ai.seo_question: What are the five pillars of Islam according to Shia hadith and who are the Imams mentioned?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi redefines the foundational pillars of Islam by elevating Wilayah to a status equal to prayer and zakat, asserting that ignorance of the Imam results in a 'death of ignorance' (mawtatan bi-jahiliyyah). It explicitly links the command to obey 'Ulil-Amr' in Surah An-Nisa to the specific lineage of the Twelve Imams, starting with Ali and proceeding through the Ahl al-Bayt, thereby establishing their divine authority as the necessary context for all other acts of worship.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Hammad Bin usman, from Isa Bin Al Sariy who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Narrate to me about what foundations Al-Islām has been built upon, so that when I take with it, my deeds would be purified and ignorance of what I do not know would not harm me, after it’.

So heasws said: ‘The testimony that there is no god except for Allahazwj and that Muhammadsaww is Rasoolsaww of Allahazwj, and the acknowledgement with whatever hesaww came with from the Presence of Allahazwj, and a right of Zakāt in the wealth, and the Wilayah which Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Commanded with, the Wilayah of the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww, for Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The one who dies and did not recognise his Imamasws would have died a death of ‘جَاهِلِيَّةً’ (Kufr - the Pre-Islāmic period).
Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Said [4:59] Obey Allah and obey the Rasool and those in authority from among you.

So it was Ali<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, then it came to be after him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, Al-Hasan<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>. Then, from after him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, Al-Husayn<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>. Then from after him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, Ali<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>. Then from after him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, Muhammad<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>.

Then that is how the matter happened to be. The earth would not be correct except with an Imamasws, and the one who dies without having recognised his Imamasws would have died the death of ‘جَاهِلِيَّةً’ (kufr - the Pre-Islāmic period); and the neediest of what one of you will ever be to hisasws recognition is when his soul reaches over here’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> pointed by his<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> hand to his<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> chest’. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘He would be saying then, ‘I was upon a beautiful matter’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Isa al-Sariyy who has said the following:

“Once I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) to teach me the principles of Islam in such a way that on holding to them my deeds can take pure and correct form and thereafter the ignorance of whatever I am ignorant of cannot harm me.

The Imam said, ‘Of the principles of Islam are to testify and acknowledge that no one deserves to be worshipped except Allah, and that Muhammad (a.s.) is the Messenger of Allah. Of such principles is to affirm and acknowledge that whatever he has brought is from Allah, to pay al-Zakat (charity) is a right and that al-Wilayah which Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has commanded to accept and acknowledge is al-Wilayah (Divine Authority) of Ahl al-Bayt of Muhammad, recipient of divine supreme covenant.
The Messenger of Allah has said, “Whoever dies while he does not know who his Imam is, he is considered as one who has died in the darkness of ignorance.”
Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said, “Obey Allah, obey the Messenger of Allah and the persons among you who possess Divine Authority.” [4:59].

Imam Ali was there (possessed Divine Authority) and after him were Imam Hassan, Imam Husayn and Ali ibn al-Husayn and after them was Muhammad ibn Ali, recipients of divine supreme covenant, successively and thus it will continue.
The land will not take an ideal shape without an Imam. Whoever dies while he does not know who his Imam is, he is considered as one who has died in the darkness of ignorance.
What everyone of you will need very urgently when his soul will reach here (pointing to his chest) is to know him (the Imam)
so that he can say it is certain that I have been holding to a genuinely good matter.”’
